title: 2026年 Gamescom 开幕夜现场亮点
content:
The highlights of Gamescom Opening Night Live 2026 | GamesIndustry.biz

GamesIndustry.biz
was at Gamescom Opening Night Live on Tuesday night, the eighth instalment of the digital showcase. The hall was packed, without an empty seat in sight, and there were plenty of gaming celebrities in attendance: Xbox head Asha Sharma could be seen near the front, gamely forming an 'X' with her arms as the camera panned over her.
Geoff Keighley opened the show with a surprisingly heartfelt speech, where he explained that after last year's event he flew back home to be with his dying father, who passed away shortly afterwards. Keighley also acknowledged the industry's troubles, saying "it's no secret that the video game industry is changing and evolving," citing widespread layoffs coupled with hardware price rises caused by the
AI components crisis
. "But in spite of all that, developers around the world are pushing forward to build new games," he said.
Nodusfall First Reveal Trailer: "Wield Divinity, Sever the Dreadnodus"
Hoyoverse kicked off the show with Nodusfall
Watch on YouTube
The show's opening trailer started by flashing up the word Hoyoverse, eliciting excited gasps from those seated around us, perhaps reflecting the global reach of titles like Genshin Impact and Honkai Star Rail. The game was Nodusfall, a highly polished co-op action title with clear similarities to Capcom's Monster Hunter franchise, as players teamed up to take down dragon-like creatures.
It was a sign of things to come, with a strong presence from Chinese and Korean companies in this year's Opening Night Live, which included titles like
Cinder City
and
Like or Die
from NC,
PUBG: Ded.Net
from Krafton,
Ananta
and
Sea of Remnants
from Netease, Zoopunk from Ti Games, and
Tides of Annihilation
from the Chengdu-based Eclipse Glow Games, not to mention another Hoyoverse title in the form of the life-simulation game Petit Planet.
Director Naoki Hamaguchi came on stage to introduce Final Fantasy 7: Revelation, which is due in spring 2027 – and is notably launching on all platforms simultaneously, whereas the previous two games were timed PlayStation exclusives.
We also saw on-stage appearances from Jon Bloch and Pavel Ulmer of 4A Games, who introduced the trailer for Metro 2039, which is due in February 2027. "Creating a game this dark requires a lot of passion, discipline, and a development team that has become accustomed to working without peace or regularity," said Bloch, while Ulmer added that the development was "pretty rough, trust me"; the trailer began by flashing up the message "Proudly made in Ukraine".
The Witcher 3: Wild Hunt — Remastered | Official Announcement Trailer
The Witcher 3 brought the house down, 11 years after its release
Watch on YouTube
But the biggest hit of the night was undoubtedly The Witcher 3, which closed proceedings. The crowd erupted at news that the game is being remastered with a raft of improvements, from improved combat to ray tracing, and that the remastered version is being given away as a free upgrade for all owners of the original game on September 29. Not only that, the game's previous two expansions are being given away for free to owners of the base game, ahead of the launch of
the third expansion
, Songs of the Past, in 2027. Level design lead Miles Tost came on stage to say CD Projekt Red had wanted to do "one more story" with Geralt for a while, and a brief look at the upcoming expansion showed Geralt with a new chain weapon.
Elsewhere in the show, Wizards of the Coast showcased the space adventure
Exodus
, due on April 7, 2027, as well as providing a lengthy gameplay trailer for the Dungeons & Dragons title
Warlock
, also due next year, but with no fixed date.
LEGO Skylines - Wishlist Trailer | gamescom 2026
The city builder Lego Skylines
Watch on YouTube
Other highlights included trailers for
Exterminauts
from Behaviour Interactive and Level Infinite, which looks like a more light-hearted take on Helldivers 2; the new city builder
Lego Skylines
, which is being published by Paradox Interactive; and
Ontos
from Frictional Games and Kepler, which was billed as a spiritual successor to Soma. We also saw a trailer for 1001 Threads of Mizan, the first game from MBC Game Studio, which is funded by the Saudi Arabian broadcast company MBC.
The absurd trailer for
Showa American Story
, featuring the game's protagonist assaulting foes with an American flag and an arm-mounted drill, garnered a smattering of applause from the crowd, indicating 4Divinity might be on to something with its strategy of
focusing on kooky AA titles
.
Stage Tour
from RedOctane, meanwhile, generated bona fide whoops, indicating that
the return of rhythm action guitar games is long overdue
.
On the subject of blasts from the past, the audience got a first look at Sega's
Crazy Taxi World Tour
, while
Turok: Origins
, developed by Saber Interactive, was confirmed to be coming in spring 2027. Heroes of Might and Magic 3, meanwhile, is
getting a remake
, some 27 years after its release in 1999.
Lofsöng World Premiere Trailer | gamescom Opening Night Live 2026
Lofsöng is by the Turin-based Unrelated Studio
Watch on YouTube
Among the indie standouts were
Lofsöng
from Unrelated Studio,
Dust: Origins
from Airship Syndicate, and Daniel Mullins' wild-looking
Pony Island 2: Panda Circus
, which is coming on April 27, 2027.
A few other highlights came in the pre-show ahead of the main event, which kicked off with the announcement of
Worms: Galactic Tactics
from Team17, an isometric turn-based tactics game due in 2027.
Rollercoaster Tycoon Wonderworks
is coming soon to Early Access, seemingly staying close to the pixel art look of the beloved original, while
Murals
from Dlala Studios stood out by securing legendary comedian Bob Mortimer for voiceover duties.

Perceptum
, due in 2027 from indie studio Duck Reaction, al
